title: Unclassified Functional Vestibular Disorders
content: Functional vestibular disorders (FVDs) are the most common cause of chronic dizziness and among the most prevalent vestibular conditions in adults, representing a significant public health concern. In 2017, the Behavioral Subcommittee of the Bárány Society’s Classification Committee established consensus-based clinical criteria for persistent postural-perceptual dizziness (PPPD)—a unifying diagnostic category that encompasses previously described FVDs, including phobic postural vertigo, space and motion discomfort, visual vertigo, and chronic subjective dizziness. Beyond these well-defined disorders lies a group of unclassified functional vestibular disorders (UFVDs), such as chronic persistent dizziness, perceptions of simultaneous movement in multiple spatial planes, and voluntary nystagmus. While these conditions share a functional (non-organic) basis, they do not meet the diagnostic criteria for established entities like PPPD. Unclassified functional vestibular disorders differ from PPPD in their inconsistent symptom patterns, variable triggers, and notably lower prevalence. Although currently under-recognized and insufficiently characterized, these disorders remain clinically relevant. A comprehensive understanding of both common and rare vestibular disorders is essential for accurate diagnosis, reducing diagnostic uncertainty, and optimizing patient management.
